common_name: Tennessee Clone Oakleaf Hydrangea (Heavy-Blooming Wild Selection)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Tennessee Clone is a naturally occurring woodland selection noted for producing an unusually heavy set of flower panicles compared with typical wild oakleaf hydrangea.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun in the Deep South. Tennessee Clone is a wild-collected selection valued above many seed-grown oakleaf hydrangeas for the sheer density of its upright, cone-shaped flower panicles, which open creamy white in early summer and age to a dusty pink as the season progresses. It keeps the bold, deeply lobed foliage, cinnamon-colored exfoliating bark, and strong burgundy-to-orange fall color typical of the species, but on a full-size, multi-stemmed frame better suited to naturalized borders and woodland edges than tight foundation plantings. Because flower buds form on the current season's growth by late summer, prune only immediately after flowering to avoid removing next year's display. Established plants tolerate average garden soil once settled in but perform best with consistent moisture during the first two seasons.
sources: Dirr, Michael A. — Manual of Woody Landscape Plants
